desc: Chinese developer of CAE simulation software for engineering design, used by industrial, automotive and electronics manufacturers.
markets: Chinese industrial, automotive, aerospace and electronics manufacturers. No verified expansion plans.
rationale: Simulation software is core to F1 aero and vehicle design; a partnership could showcase domestic CAE credibility to Chinese engineering buyers.

desc: Hong Kong-listed group whose name and assigned sector point to new-energy or clean-power activities; business not verified.
markets: Not verified. No verified expansion plans.
rationale: Unclear; a new-energy group could use F1 sustainability themes for B2B visibility if its business is confirmed.

desc: Indian maker of payment cards, identity documents and card personalisation services, part of the Manipal Technologies group.
markets: Banks, payment networks and government identity programmes in India and nearby markets. No verified expansion plans.
rationale: Secure payment and identity technology could be showcased to bank and fintech buyers; limited consumer angle.

desc: Chinese provider of cloud ERP and SaaS tools for e-commerce merchants managing orders, inventory and multi-platform sales.
markets: Chinese online merchants and brands selling across e-commerce platforms. No verified expansion plans.
rationale: Newly listed SaaS brand could use F1 hospitality and visibility in China to court larger merchant and brand customers.

desc: Indonesian pulp and paper maker producing writing paper, stationery and office paper, part of Asia Pulp & Paper.
markets: Exports paper and stationery products to Asia, the Middle East, Africa, Europe and the Americas. No verified expansion plans.
rationale: Packaging and paper are a weak fit; stationery brands could gain limited awareness in export markets.
flags: part of the Sinar Mas / Asia Pulp & Paper group

desc: Chinese seed company breeding and selling hybrid rice, corn and vegetable seeds, with a corn seed business in Brazil.
markets: Chinese farmers plus a corn seed operation in Brazil; also seed sales in South and Southeast Asia.
rationale: Agricultural seeds have little F1 fit; the Brazil business offers only marginal brand value around the São Paulo race.

desc: Indonesian palm oil plantation and refining company selling cooking oil, margarine and oleochemical products under brands such as Filma.
markets: Indonesian consumers and food manufacturers; exports palm oil products across Asia and beyond. No verified expansion plans.
rationale: Palm oil carries reputational issues in sponsorship; consumer cooking-oil brands are domestic, so F1 fit is weak.

desc: Chinese chip designer of RF beamforming and phased-array transceiver chips for satellite communications and radar systems.
markets: Chinese satellite communication, radar and defence-related customers. No verified expansion plans.
rationale: Specialist defence and satellite RF chips have few F1 uses and little need for global brand marketing.

desc: South Korean maker of semiconductor test handlers and inspection equipment used by memory chipmakers in back-end testing.
markets: Memory and chip makers in South Korea, the US, China and Southeast Asia. No verified expansion plans.
rationale: Niche chip-equipment supplier sells to a handful of chipmakers; F1 hospitality offers limited value.

desc: Norwegian maker of Pure-Pak paper cartons and filling machines for milk, juice and other liquid foods.
markets: Dairy and juice producers in Europe, the Americas, the Middle East and Asia; new US plant in Arkansas.
rationale: Renewable cartons could support sustainability messaging with beverage producers, but it has little consumer visibility.

desc: Chinese maker of slot-die coating heads and coating equipment used in lithium-ion battery electrode manufacturing.
markets: Chinese battery manufacturers. No verified expansion plans.
rationale: Precision coating tools for battery makers could link to F1 hybrid themes, but the customer base is narrow.

desc: Taiwanese fabless designer of power-management chips, including PWM controllers and MOSFETs for PCs, graphics cards and servers.
markets: PC, graphics card and server makers in Taiwan, China and elsewhere in Asia. No verified expansion plans.
rationale: Small fabless supplier to PC makers; F1 offers little beyond occasional B2B hospitality.

desc: Paper-based packaging group making containerboard, corrugated boxes and consumer packaging for customers in Europe and the Americas.
markets: Consumer goods, food, e-commerce and industrial customers across Europe, North America and Latin America.
rationale: Packaging buyers are large consumer brands; F1 hospitality could support key-account relationships and sustainability messaging.

desc: Chinese maker of automotive wheel hub bearing units, largely for the aftermarket and exported to North America.
markets: Auto parts aftermarket in North America and Europe plus Chinese customers. No verified expansion plans.
rationale: Aftermarket parts brand could gain credibility with distributors via motorsport, but it is a small exporter.

desc: Chilean forestry, pulp, paper, packaging and tissue group whose Softys unit sells Elite and Babysec brands.
markets: Pulp exported worldwide; tissue and packaging in Chile, Brazil, Argentina, Mexico, Peru and other Latin American markets.
rationale: Softys tissue brands could use F1 visibility in Brazil and Mexico races, but the core is commodity pulp.

desc: Chinese MEMS chip foundry and process developer serving sensor, communications and biomedical device makers.
markets: MEMS chip customers in China and internationally. No verified expansion plans.
rationale: Specialist foundry with narrow customer base; F1 brand value is limited to technology credibility.

desc: Malaysian palm oil plantation group also producing oleochemicals and developing property, with plantations in Malaysia and Indonesia.
markets: Plantations in Malaysia, Indonesia and Liberia; oleochemical plants in Asia and Europe selling worldwide.
rationale: Commodity plantation group with no consumer brand; palm oil is a reputational risk for sponsorship.

desc: Chinese steel processing and distribution company supplying cut and formed sheet steel to automotive and appliance manufacturers.
markets: Chinese automotive and home appliance manufacturers. No verified expansion plans.
rationale: Steel processing for carmakers has little F1 marketing logic; at most B2B hospitality.

desc: Israeli travel company whose name and assigned sector indicate airline ticketing and tour services; details not verified.
markets: Israeli travellers. No verified expansion plans.
rationale: Travel brand could sell race travel packages to Israeli fans, but it is small and domestic.
